- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast shows upward bias, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% relative to recent high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >1.5% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect; cap forecast decline to 0.8x prior peak or reduce by 0.3–0.5% per day.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.3) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast by 0.3–0.7% to align with momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 0.8x of 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid over-optimism in early days; first 5–7 days should be conservative (±0.5% below true mean of prior 18 days).
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly negative and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 0.2–0.4% per day to avoid “over-leverage” bias.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more), forecast should be capped at ±0.5% of recent 7-day range to avoid overfitting.
